$comment: Places where a cited DEV/ADR id has no entry, with a reason AND a kind.
kind: 'deliberate-mention' — the id is named IN ORDER to say it is missing,
or the file is a verbatim archive whose text must not be rewritten. These
kind: 'deferred-fix' — the citation IS wrong and reads as a real
cross-reference, but fixing it is blocked on something outside this file.
These require a `tracked` task id and are printed on every run so they
cannot quietly become permanent. An allowlist that cannot tell these apart
converts real errors into permitted ones, which is the failure mode the
verifier identified when this file was introduced.
Scoped by file, not file:line, so the allowlist survives edits above a
citation. The cost is a whole-file blast radius: a NEW wrong citation of the
same id in an allowlisted file is suppressed silently. Keep the list short.

allow.reason: The verifier's remit uses DEV.38 as the worked example of why the dangling check exists — a citation that propagated from a prompt into three documents, and that meant two different things in different places.

COVERS THREE SITES, and only the first is wrong — stated here because the entry is file-scoped and its previous reason described only one of them. (1) PROJECT_PLAN.md:90, the hand-maintained Stage B B.10 row, cites DEV.38 for a Day 8 seed cross-tenant dealer bug whose entry was never written (F.72, DEV.128). That citation IS wrong and reads as a real cross-reference. (2) and (3) lines 285 and 292 are generated by pnpm plan:sync from F.63's and F.72's notes, which name DEV.38 in order to say it is missing — deliberate mentions, equivalent to the DEV.41/DEV.42 entries for this file, and correct as they stand. Site (1) is NOT corrected here because it sits outside the STAGE_F_TASKS markers, in the region the verifier requires to be byte-identical against main — so this check and that one are in genuine tension. The operator decided explicitly not to overrule: DEV.112's overrule was justified by unsatisfiability, whereas this is avoidable, F.63 fixes it next, and the wrong citation is inert meanwhile. Spending an overrule here would establish that two checks in tension is grounds for bypass. WHEN F.63 LANDS this entry is CONVERTED to kind: deliberate-mention, not deleted — sites (2) and (3) survive as legitimate generated mentions, so deleting it would make them newly dangling.
